messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran a 30m synthetic burst against canary nodes to reproduce the tail we saw yesterday. Wanted to share numbers and get ideas for mitigations.

sara: nice, what were the p95/p99 numbers during the burst vs baseline? :eyes:

alex: baseline (steady state): p50 40ms, p95 190ms, p99 320ms. During burst: p50 48ms, p95 280ms, p99 720ms. Big increase at the tail.

jonas: ugh 720ms p99. Any correlation with KV miss rate or kernel fallbacks?

alex: yes — KV miss fraction jumped from 2% -> ~18% during the high QPS window. Also seeing repeated log lines where kernel-selector falls back to the generic kernel after a few microbatches.

mike: do you have an example of the fallback logs?

alex: pasted snippet from canary logs: ```[2026-02-14T14:12:03Z] kernel_selector: chosen=fast_attn_bs2, microbatch=1 -> fallback=generic_attn_bs1, reason=inefficient_batch_shape```

jonas: that fallback explains a lot. Fast kernels require microbatch >=2 to hit vectorized path. If autoscaler spawns nodes but microbatch sizes shrink (lots of single-request microbatches), selector flips to slower kernels and tail spikes.

sara: how long is the scale-up lag? is the broker queueing requests and then microbatcher collapsing them?

alex: measured scale-up median = 14s, 95th = 38s. During that window, request rate per instance is tiny so microbatcher often emits small batches. Combined with cold KV (misses) we see both kernel slowdown and KV fetch latencies stacking.

devex-amber: do we have profiler traces for a representative cold-path p99? want flamegraph to see if it's NVLink stalls vs CPU/IO.

alex: uploaded traces to s3://redwood-prod-profiles/2001234567/canary/ — key files: burst_p99_perf.folded and nvtx_trace.json. TL;DR: ~60% of extra time is in kv fetch (~remote read + serialization), ~30% in slower kernel GEMM path.

mike: interesting. So two levers: reduce KV cold misses (preheat/prefetch), and avoid kernel fallback by encouraging microbatch >=2 or changing kernel threshold. Which is cheaper?

jonas: we can try a small kernel-selector tweak: prefer fast_attn even at microbatch=1 for sequences <64 (our burst seq distribution is short). It's a quick patch and should reduce kernel contribution to p99. But if a request truly needs the generic kernel, we need guardrails.

sara: what's the risk? incorrect numerical error or OOM?

jonas: risk is minimal for short sequences; we've validated numeric parity for a couple models. OOM risk only if memory assumptions change — keep a safety check to revert.

alex: I prototyped a selector override on the canary: forced fast_attn for seq<=64. Result: p99 fell from 720ms -> 510ms during burst. Not perfect but helps. KV still accounts for large chunk.

mike: for KV -> preheat runway, what did you test? Increasing prober sampling or extending preheat TTL?

alex: tested two approaches: 1) prober smoothing (increase sampling window to 45s so warm nodes get re-probed more aggressively), 2) keep-alive prefetch on scale-up (run a tiny warmup request that touches KV prefixes for active models). The keep-alive prefetch dropped KV miss fraction from 18% -> 6% and p99 down to ~380ms.

devex-amber: nice. Any observable cost delta? prefetch adds a tiny token cost and a few ms per new instance. CPU overhead negligible.

alex: rough numbers: +0.3% cost for prefetch traffic vs ~25% improvement in tail. Worth it for canary / high-SLO routes.

sara: autoscaler settings — can we adjust burst capacity or add a short warm-hot pool to absorb surges?

jonas: we could keep a small warm pool at 5% standby for tier-1 customers. That avoids full cold path but costs baseline reservation. Alternatively, speed up scale-up by priming GPU process startup (skip heavy JIT on first request).

mike: is there an easy runtime tweak to reduce process init time? maybe parallelize kernel link stage.

alex: we've already parallelized parts, but some 3rd-party ops introduce blocking. Short term: the keep-alive prefetch is lowest friction. Medium term: kernel link parallelization + lazy JIT to delay heavy work till after first response.

devex-amber: what about microbatch policy — can we bias microbatcher to wait 10ms to collect a second request during bursts? that will increase p50 slightly but can dramatically cut kernel fallback frequency.

jonas: yes, a short batching window helps. We tested wait=8ms at 95% load and saw microbatch rate of >=2 for 70% of windows; p95 improved by ~60ms and p99 by ~120ms. Tradeoff: added latency to p50 by ~6ms.

sara: need to decide for SLOs. for low-latency routes maybe keep default, for bursty but less latency-sensitive ones enable wait. Could be route-configurable.

alex: next steps I propose: 1) roll kernel-selector override to canary for seq<=64 with safety kill, 2) enable keep-alive prefetch on scale-up in canary, 3) experiment microbatch wait=8ms on candidate routes, 4) monitor tail metrics and KV miss fraction. I'll open a quick PR and an observability dashboard.

mike: sounds good. Can you add the rollback metric (kernel fallback rate) to the alert runbook?

alex: yes will do. Also adding an experiment tag so we can roll back if p50 regresses beyond 10ms.

infra-bot: deploy-canary started by alex at 2026-02-14T15:02:00Z — image: runtime:2026.02.14-canary-abc123

sara: thanks everyone. If the canary numbers look good in the next 2 hours we can promote. :thumbsup:

jonas: +1, and I'll prototype a small autoscaler tweak to reduce scale-up cold-start time in parallel.

alex: will post the PR and the dashboard link in this thread when ready. Thanks all. :rocket:
